A header-only file also raises IndexError, because `rows` then has only one element.

The whole-word check uses `(?<!\w)` and `(?!\w)` around the pattern. Word boundary uses `(?<!\w)` / `(?!\w)`, so underscores and digits count as word characters. Also, with re.IGNORECASE the match uses regex case-insensitivity rather than casefold, which differs from the other matchers (e.g. `ß`/`SS`). Patterns that begin or end with a non-word character (e.g. `AT&T `, `C&A.`) are handled by lookarounds that are stricter than 'word boundaries'.
